title: What If Every Kelp Forest in the Ocean Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every kelp forest vanished? It grows a foot a day.
Kelp is already in trouble. In 2014 to 2016, more than 90 percent of bull kelp in Northern California was lost.
The cause is a chain reaction. Purple sea urchins exploded in number, up more than 10,000 percent on the North Coast.
Urchins strip the seafloor into barrens, and those barrens can last for decades.
Fish, invertebrates and even marine mammals lose food and shelter. The red urchin fishery collapsed and the abalone fishery closed.
Kelp forests also store carbon, about 20 times more per acre than forests on land, so losing them removes a coastal buffer too.
